title: Burns' tours collapse in Kentucky
summary: Burns' later bookings dry up, the cars break down in Kentucky and the band returns to Tulsa broke.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Rene was still with you then?

Yeah, Rene was still with me then. He was with the band eight years. We played several dates for Burns and all at once it just stopped, but he didn't leave me out entirely, he told me he didn't have anything so you better go on back. So anyway, I went on back and I got a call from Burns again maybe a month or two later and he was sending me in a different direction this time. I don't know if you've ever been on one, but this is really--took the cake--I don't think I did two dates this time, but all at once he just faded. We were travelling in two cars, and one of the cars was pulling a trailer with the instruments, we played Springfield, Missouri--I'll never forget--we were heading east a little, I think a little town in Kentucky.

We played that engagement and I was---we had car trouble, and I mean serious, bearings or something and no money and this and that and it was in the wintertime. I was waiting to hear from Burns and I didn't hear anything so I said to the men, well I'll tell you what, whether he has dates or whatever he has, I said we're going to pile up some kind of way in this car and hook the trailer on this. I think it was the car that was pulling the trailer that broke down. I said we'll come back later and make some arrangements to get the car; we got to get out of here, we're not going to spend what money we have here.
So we came on back to Tulsa and I believe it was six months or a year that I didn't hear from Harry Burns--
(Side A of Tape 5 ended at this point. Transcript will continue in accordance with Side B.)
